citation: Danjong Sillok vol.4 (Taebaeksan copy 2책 4권 20장B; Guksa-pyeonchan facsimile 6책 556면); https://sillok.history.go.kr/id/kfa_10012007_001
date_original: 端宗卽位年 12月 7日 乙未
original_text: 霧, 咫尺不辨人, 木氷。
english: Fog; one could not make out a person at arm's length. Rime on the trees.
reading: Ordinary midwinter fog and rime. Before any expected aerosol effect.

date_original: 端宗卽位年 12月 10日 戊戌
original_text: 大雪, 深三四尺, 鳥獸飢, 多入人家。
english: Heavy snow, three to four chi deep. Birds and beasts starved and many came into people's houses.
reading: Severe winter snow, winter 1452/53. Severe but in season.

date_original: 端宗卽位年 12月 28日 丙辰
original_text: 霧。木氷。
english: Fog. Rime on the trees.
reading: Ordinary winter weather.

date_original: 端宗 1年 6月 28日 癸丑
original_text: 雨雪于咸吉道咸興府。
english: Rain and snow fell at Hamheung-bu in Hamgil province.
reading: Snow in early August at a coastal city near 40° N. The text says only that it happened; it does not say the sky was dim. A summer cold anomaly, consistent with (not diagnostic of) aerosol cooling.

date_original: 端宗 1年 7月 13日 戊辰
original_text: 甲山郡隕霜三日, 寒氣如十月。
english: At Gapsan county frost fell for three days, and the cold was like the tenth month.
reading: Late-summer frost and cold. Gapsan sits high on the Gaema plateau, where August frost is less rare; the court still recorded it as unusual ('like the tenth month').

date_original: 端宗 1年 10月 21日
date_method: computed (no ganzhi on this row; first article of day carries it)
original_text: 江原道諸邑, 因雨水、早霜, 失農爲甚, 明年種食, 過半不給。
english: In the counties of Gangwon province, because of rain and early frost, the harvest failed badly; for next year, seed and food will fall short by more than half.
reading: The 1453 growing season in Gangwon was ended early by frost. Date is the date of the report, not of the frost.

date_original: 端宗 2年 3月 12日 癸亥
original_text: 陰霧四塞, 翼日亦如之。
english: A gloomy fog filled all four quarters, and the next day was the same.
reading: Could be spring dust haze or fog. No colour of the sun given. Weak.

date_original: 端宗 2年 2月 24日 乙巳
original_text: 大風雨雪, 景福宮、光化門扉裂。
english: A great wind with rain and snow; the doors of Gyeongbok Palace and Gwanghwa Gate split.
reading: Late-March snowstorm. In season for Seoul; weak.

citation: Danjong Sillok vol.14 (5책 14권 15장B; 7책 36면); https://sillok.history.go.kr/id/kfa_10304024_001 (and five more frost notices, 1455-05-11 to 05-18)
date_original: 端宗 3年 4月 24日 己亥
place: Jeolla province, 12 counties (Unbong, Okgwa, Heungyang, Jangsu, Sunchang, Gwangju, ...)
original_text: 隕霜于全羅道雲峯、玉果、興陽、長水、淳昌、光州、長城、礪山、鎭安、珍山、泰仁、任實。
english: Frost fell in Jeolla province at Unbong, Okgwa, Heungyang, Jangsu, Sunchang, Gwangju, Jangseong, Yeosan, Jinan, Jinsan, Taein and Imsil.
reading: Mid-May frost across southern Korea, two years after onset. Fits lingering cold (MXD stays negative through 1455) but is not an onset marker.

citation: Ming Yingzong Shilu juan 213; sillok.history.go.kr id msilok_005_2130_0010_0010_0080_0010
date_original: 景泰三年 二月 八日
original_text: 茲當仲春少陽用事之時而寒氣脅之古占以為人君刑法暴濫之象近恒寒也
english: Now in mid-spring, when the lesser yang should rule, cold air oppresses it; the ancient omen-texts take this as a sign of a ruler's harsh punishments; it approaches 'persistent cold'.
reading: Spring 1452 cold, in a memorial about portents. Before the earliest plausible aerosol arrival unless the eruption was in 1451/early 1452. Rhetorical context.

date_original: 景泰三年 十月 三十日
place: Taihe county, Yingzhou, Fengyang prefecture (Huai valley)
original_text: 直隷鳳陽府潁州太和縣奏今春雨雪連綿二麥無收秋又積雨
english: Taihe county (Yingzhou, Fengyang) reported: this spring rain and snow went on and on and the wheat and barley yielded nothing; in autumn there was again heavy rain.
reading: Wet, cold spring 1452 in the Huai valley. Precedes the 1453 sulfate onset.

date_original: 景泰四年 正月 二十八日
original_text: 去年各處旱澇荐臻人民飢饉畿內三冬少雪二麥鮮收
english: Last year drought and flood came again and again everywhere and the people starved; in the capital region the three winter months had little snow, and the wheat and barley yielded little.
reading: North China winter 1452/53 was dry, not cold-snowy.

date_original: 景泰四年 正月 二十九日
original_text: 邇者新春風雨連月寒沍倍冬
english: Recently, in the new spring, wind and rain have gone on for a month, and the freezing cold is twice that of winter.
reading: Earliest 1453 cold statement found in the Ming Shilu. A memorial on portents, so the wording may be heightened.

citation: juan 233; id msilok_005_2330_0010_0010_0100_0030; also Mingshi juan 28 (雨雪隕霜)
date_original: report 景泰四年 九月 十一日; event 景泰四年 二月–三月
place: Eight guards of Fengyang (Zhongdu), Huai valley
original_text: 中都留守司所屬鳳陽府八衛各奏今年二月三月雨雪不止麥苗浥爛
english: The eight guards of Fengyang under the Zhongdu garrison each reported: this year in the second and third months snow fell without stopping, and the wheat seedlings rotted.
reading: Spring snow at 33° N lasting into lunar month 3 (to early May Julian). The 'spring 1453 nonstop snow' that Pang 1993 cites. Ordinary late snow is possible; two months is not ordinary.

date_original: 景泰四年 七月 一日 (event 六月)
place: Datong/Shuozhou (hail); Huai, Henan, Shandong (rain); Shuntian, Baoding, Shanxi (drought)
original_text: 直隷鳳陽淮安府徐州河南開封衛輝南陽山東袞青萊諸府各奏自五月以來滛雨連綿…順天府直隷保定府萬全都司山西太原府各奏亢旱不雨大同府朔州奏六月雨雹傷民禾稼
english: Fengyang, Huai'an, Xuzhou, Kaifeng, Weihui, Nanyang, Yanzhou, Qingzhou and Laizhou each reported continuous excessive rain since the fifth month ... Shuntian, Baoding, Wanquan and Taiyuan each reported severe drought without rain; Datong and Shuozhou reported hail in the sixth month that damaged crops.
reading: Summer 1453 in China: wet south of the Yellow River, dry north. No cold or sky anomaly stated.

source: Ming Yingzong Shilu; Mingshi juan 28 (恆寒)
citation: Shilu juan 238, id msilok_005_2380_0010_0010_0240_0020 (Wang Hong memorial, rec. 景泰五年二月二十六日); Mingshi juan 28 Wuxing 1 恆寒, https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/明史/卷28
date_original: event from 景泰四年 十一月 十六日 (Mingshi: 十一月戊辰) to 景泰五年 正月
date_method: computed; Mingshi ganzhi 戊辰 = day 16 independently
category: extreme cold: snow + sea ice + mass freezing deaths
place: Shandong, Henan, Zhejiang, Zhili, Huai and Xu; the sea east of the Huai
original_text: 十一月十六日至今正月大雪瀰漫平地数尺朔風峻急飄瓦摧垣淮河東海冰結四十餘里人民頭畜凍死不下萬計 | Mingshi: 景泰四年冬十一月戊辰至明年孟春，山東、河南、浙江、直隸、淮、徐大雪數尺，淮東之海冰四十餘里，人畜凍死萬計
english: From the 16th of the 11th month until this first month, heavy snow lay everywhere, several chi deep on the flat; the north wind was fierce, blowing off tiles and breaking walls; the Huai river and the eastern sea froze for more than forty li; people and livestock frozen to death numbered no fewer than ten thousand. | Mingshi: From the wuchen day of the 11th month, winter of Jingtai 4, to the first month of spring of the next year, in Shandong, Henan, Zhejiang, Zhili, Huai and Xu heavy snow lay several chi deep; the sea east of the Huai froze for more than forty li; people and animals frozen to death numbered in the tens of thousands.
reading: The winter 1453/54 disaster. Start date is fixed to 15 Dec 1453 (Julian) by two independent day-forms. Severe and widespread to 27° N, but a cold-air outbreak, not a sky phenomenon.

date_original: 景泰五年 四月 五日 (丙戌)
original_text: 山東地方自去冬至今春隆寒沍凍魚鼈亦死草不萌三月初氷猶不解
english: In Shandong, from last winter to this spring, there was intense cold and hard frost; even fish and turtles died, the grass did not sprout, and at the start of the third month the ice still had not melted.
reading: Cold persisting into April 1454.

date_original: 景泰五年 六月 十九日 (report)
original_text: 湖廣衡州府奏去冬至今春雨雪連綿兼以疫癘本府所隸一州八縣人民死者一萬八千七百四十七口凍死牛三萬六千七百八十五隻
english: Hengzhou prefecture in Huguang reported: from last winter to this spring rain and snow went on and on, with epidemic disease besides; in the one sub-prefecture and eight counties under the prefecture 18,747 people died, and 36,785 oxen froze to death.
reading: Cold reached 27° N in winter 1453/54.

date_original: 景泰五年 三月 十日 (report)
original_text: 江南蘇常等府積雪民凍餓使者甚多常熟一縣至一千八百餘人
english: In Suzhou, Changzhou and other prefectures of Jiangnan snow lay deep and very many people died of cold and hunger; in Changshu county alone more than 1,800.
reading: Winter 1453/54 in the lower Yangtze.

date_original: 景泰五年 十月 二十九日 (memorial)
original_text: 也今亦或死氷 日或昏蝕風非淡蕩天之示灾
english: ... now some even died of ice; the sun is at times dim or eclipsed, the wind is not gentle: these are Heaven's warnings of calamity.
reading: The only 'dim sun' wording found in China 1452–54, and it sits in a list of portents in a memorial with no date or place. Not usable as an observation.

source: Oliński 2016, citing Annales Glogovienses, Sigismundus Rosicz chronica, N. Pol (Jahrbücher der Stadt Breslau)
citation: P. Oliński, 'O opisach pogody przez Jana Długosza w Annales', in Jan Długosz (1415–1480): życie i dzieła, Kraków 2016, p. 202 and n. 17; https://repozytorium.umk.pl/handle/item/5144
date_original: winter 1453/1454, 23 XI – 15 XII
original_text: [Polish, Oliński:] 'Według źródeł śląskich wyjątkowo mroźna była pierwsza faza zimy 1453/1454: od 23 XI do 15 XII'
english: 'According to Silesian sources the first phase of the winter of 1453/1454 was exceptionally frosty: from 23 November to 15 December.'
reading: Central European cold spell in the same weeks as the Huai freeze (from 15 Dec). Secondhand: the chronicle text itself was not read.

source: Oliński 2016, citing Długosz Annales lib. XII p.224; Oliwa chronicle
date_original: winter 1454/1455
original_text: Długosz: 'hiems quoque validissima, nivibus eciam illam augentibus' | Oliwa: Baltic froze as far as Hel
english: Długosz: 'the winter too was very severe, and snows made it worse still.' | The Oliwa chronicle records the Baltic frozen as far as Hel.
reading: Second post-onset winter. Oliński adds (p. 207) that Polish sources give no information on unusual colouring of the sun or clouds in these years.

source: Therrell, Stahle & Acuña-Soto 2004, BAMS 85:1263, citing Chimalpahin, Codex en Cruz (Dibble 1981), Anales de Tlatelolco
date_original: Aztec years 12 Flint (1452), 13 House (1453), 1 Rabbit (1454)
date_method: Aztec year-count correlation as given by the authors
original_text: Codex en Cruz 1453 (Dibble): 'a blackened circle from which a shower of dots falls over a maize plant ... The shower of dots can indicate snow, hail, frost, dust, or the heat of the sun.' Chimalpahin for 1452: 'This was the third year in which there was hunger. Then there was drought and hunger in Mexico.'
english: (English in source.)
reading: The famine of One Rabbit (1454) follows a drought that began by 1450–52, before the 1453 sulfate. The 1453 'killing autumn frost' is Dibble's reading of a pictograph that could also mean drought; Therrell et al. themselves favour drought. The 1453 bristlecone frost ring (LaMarche & Hirschboeck 1984) is independent support for a late-summer freeze in western North America.
